Location: While this position is posted in a specific location, all of Oyster’s positions are fully remote and you can work from home. Forever. To create the best experience for our new hire, this role requires you to be based within +5 / -5 UTC.

Role Summary

Oyster is looking for a Director of FP&A and Analytics to lead our newly consolidated FP&A and Analytics team. This role is responsible for delivering the financial insight, planning, and analytical capabilities that enable better business decisions as Oyster enters its next phase of growth.

Partnering closely with business leaders and the VP of FP&A, you will lead planning and forecasting, business performance analysis, pricing strategy, and reporting while driving the evolution of our systems, automation, and AI-enabled ways of working. You'll build a high-performing team that provides trusted insights, challenges assumptions, and improves decision quality across the business.

Key Responsibilities

 - Lead the annual planning, quarterly forecasting, and performance management processes, ensuring financial plans support business priorities and decision-making.

 - Partner with senior leaders across the business to provide financial insight, challenge assumptions, and influence strategic and operational decisions.

 - Lead financial modelling and business case development to evaluate strategic initiatives, investments, and commercial opportunities.

 - Lead the preparation of financial reporting and performance insights for monthly business reviews, Board materials, and investor updates.

 - Drive financial discipline and accountability through robust forecasting, performance analysis, and meaningful spend visibility.

 - Lead pricing analytics and commercial insights, governing pricing decisions through the Deal Desk framework.

 - Drive the adoption of AI, automation, and scalable workflows to improve forecasting, reporting, and analytical capability.

 - Lead the evolution of FP&A systems and business reporting ensuring trusted, scalable data and a single source of truth across the business.

 - Build, lead, coach, and develop a high-performing FP&A and Analytics team, fostering strong business partnership and continuous improvement.

 - Partner on strategic initiatives, due diligence, and M&A activity as required.



Core Requirements

 - 8+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, Corporate Finance, or Strategic Finance, with increasing leadership responsibility.

 - Experience leading and developing high-performing teams within a global, remote-first environment.

 - Demonstrated experience leading company-wide planning, forecasting, and business performance processes in a high-growth business.

 - Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders through data-driven financial insight and strong business partnering.

 - Strong commercial acumen with a deep understanding of SaaS business models, recurring revenue metrics, unit economics, and growth drivers.

 - Strong understanding of financial statements, cash flow management, foreign exchange, and accounting principles.

 - Experience driving improvements in finance systems, reporting, and business intelligence to enable scalable decision-making.

 - Demonstrated experience applying AI and automation to improve finance processes and analytical capabilities.

 - Experience with business intelligence and planning tools; Looker experience is a plus.



You'll also need

 - A reliable home internet connection and fluency in both written and spoken English

 - Utilize data-driven insights to understand customer needs and preferences, advocating for their interests within the organization.

 - Collaborate with the  Sales team to ensure customer retention, particularly in churn-risk situations.

 - Collaborate with Treasury on payment collection for late-paying customers

 - Stay abreast of product updates and industry trends, continuously enhancing your skills and knowledge to better serve our customers.

 - Cross-functional collaboration skills with experience working across departments to achieve common goals.

Location: While this position is posted in a specific location, all of Oyster’s positions are fully remote and you can work from home. Forever. We're open to candidates based anywhere in the AMER or EMEA regions.

Role Summary

We are hiring a content marketing lead to set the company-wide direction for Oyster’s editorial narrative: the category story we tell about the future of work, the arguments our executives make in public, and the original research that HR, Finance, and Legal leaders cite when making decisions.

You will operate as an AI-first functional lead rather than a traditional editorial manager. There are no direct reports, deliberately. Your leverage will come from the AI systems and governance you design—research agents, brand-voice models, fact-checking, source verification, repurposing, and evaluation—plus the senior stakeholders, freelancers, agencies, and subject-matter experts you mobilize.

We are looking for the person who wants to find out how much editorial ambition one exceptional operator with a well-built AI stack can carry, and who will set the standard for what an AI-native content function looks like. The scope is unusual for a single role: a live audience across our library, newsletter, and podcast; a leadership team that publishes and speaks; proprietary employment data from 180+ countries; and the mandate to build this function the way it should be built, not the way it has always been done.

Key Responsibilities

Own the narrative

 - Define Oyster’s long-term editorial and category strategy across Marketing, executive leadership, Product, People, Legal, and customer-facing teams.

 - Resolve high-stakes narrative trade-offs and establish the positions, evidence standards, and language Oyster uses consistently across business areas.

 - Own a multi-year editorial roadmap and a focused portfolio of flagship research and thought-leadership bets linked to company strategy.

 - Act as the final quality bar for voice, accuracy, evidence, and taste across human- and AI-produced content.



Build company-wide AI content mechanisms

 - Architect and govern reusable systems for research, brand voice, fact-checking, source verification, repurposing, evaluation, and reporting.

 - Define risk-based rules for where AI leads, where humans lead, and where specialist or executive approval is mandatory.

 - Establish mechanisms and standards adopted across Marketing and relevant partner teams, not only within the content workflow.

 - Measure leverage through throughput, cycle time, cost, adoption, quality, and business impact; evolve the system each quarter.

Lead thought leadership and executive voice

 - Set the operating model for executive publishing and advise leaders on the arguments Oyster should make publicly.

 - Turn proprietary employment, salary, and hiring data into a durable original-research programme that shapes external conversation.

 - Mobilize newsletter, podcast, events, PR, analyst relations, Product Marketing, partner/customer storytelling, and social around shared narratives.

Own business impact

 - Connect editorial and narrative decisions to company growth, customer trust, target-account engagement, earned influence, and pipeline.

 - Build reporting that enables executives and teams to make better portfolio and investment decisions.

 - Identify emerging market shifts early and recommend company responses before they become obvious.

Mobilize the extended organization

 - Set direction for senior stakeholders, freelancers, agencies, specialists, and subject-matter experts without relying on formal authority.

 - Create decision rights, operating rhythms, and shared standards that enable multiple teams to execute consistently.

 - Define the long-term roadmap and future organizational shape of the capability, including what remains expert-led, becomes a system, or requires hiring.



Core Requirements

 - 8+ years in content, editorial, or brand journalism, including senior ownership of a brand narrative or thought leadership programme at a B2B technology company.

 - Evidence of setting a company or category narrative that changed decisions, earned external authority, and was adopted across teams.

 - A portfolio of work that earned attention on merit through citations, quotations, debate, or organic sharing.

 - A demonstrated AI-first practice beyond drafting, including agents, custom workflows, evaluation, QA, governance, and adoption by others.

 - Exceptional English-language editorial judgment, writing, editing, sourcing, and voice control.

 - Ability to turn proprietary data and complex research into clear, defensible arguments with business relevance.

 - Experience making high-leverage trade-offs and setting direction across executives and multiple functions without formal authority.

 - Proven ability to build scalable mechanisms, operating standards, and roadmaps that enable others to deliver consistently.

 - Genuine motivation to operate as a high-autonomy IC with no direct reports and company-critical scope.
   
   

Bonus

 - Domain background in HR tech, global employment, future of work, fintech, or another compliance-heavy category.

 - Experience with AI search visibility — optimising for how assistants retrieve, summarise, and cite sources.

 - Multimedia range: video, podcast, or design fluency.

 - Experience standing up an in-house newsroom or an original research programme.

 - You have worked or lived across multiple markets, or speak more than one language.
   
   

This might not be right for you if...

 - You want a people-management role now rather than a high-autonomy IC remit.

 - Your AI experience is primarily prompting for drafts rather than building and evaluating systems.

 - You prefer high-volume production to a small portfolio of high-conviction work.

 - You are uncomfortable challenging vague, unsourced, or off-voice work—including work from senior stakeholders.

 - You need a tightly defined execution plan rather than shaping a function under ambiguity.
   
   

You'll also need

 - A reliable home internet connection and fluency in both written and spoken English

 - Provide pragmatic, solutions-focused guidance on high-risk and sensitive cases, including performance management, misconduct, investigations, and terminations

 - Navigate nuanced local legal frameworks with confidence, ensuring compliance while supporting business objectives

 - Partner closely with internal stakeholders and Oyster customers to deliver clear, actionable advice on complex people issues in a timely and commercially-minded way



Country HR information and knowledge

 - Leverage AI and automation tools to streamline the generation, updating, and scaling of country-specific HR documentation, ensuring rapid and accurate knowledge delivery.

 - Answer questions (in the form of tickets) on HR topics which are unable to be resolved by our Lifecycle Operations teams.

 - Provide internal Oyster teams with training (or other methods of increasing their knowledge) on HR topics as needs arise.

 - Look for opportunities to proactively improve country-specific HR information.

 - Attend customer calls when there are questions on country-specific HR information.

 - Work with other teams (e.g. Customer Support, Sales, Product, Legal) to problem-solve country-specific issues with your HR knowledge.

 - Continuously audit and refine workflows and ways of working to reduce response times and elevate service quality.

 - Actively leverage AI responsibly to maximize personal output, sharing best practices with the broader People Services team.

 - Analyze recurring ticket trends and received queries to identify systemic issues, proactively building preventative resources for internal teams.



Projects

 - Lead People Services and cross-functional projects as we work towards our Mission to enable companies to hire anyone, anywhere!

 - Deep employee relations expertise across multiple countries, with hands-on experience handling complex and high-risk cases (e.g. investigations, PIPs, terminations)

 - 6+ years of ER & HR generalist experience, with a strong track record of supporting both internal stakeholders and external clients

 - Portuguese, Italian and/or Spanish language skills would set you up for success in this role.

 - Cross-country HR experience, with a deep global focus (eg, APAC, EMEA, AMER, LATAM). Experience in countries like France would be a big bonus!

 - Culturally aware, with a nuanced understanding of local HR practices, norms, and expectations across the regions you’ve supported

 - Solution-oriented and commercially minded, offering well-reasoned options and confident recommendations when faced with challenging people matters

 - Skilled at stakeholder engagement, including presenting confidently to senior leaders, clients, and cross-functional teams

 - Change-ready and growth-driven, excited by ambiguity and eager to challenge the status quo to improve processes and outcomes
